You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: numa-enable-documentation
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/numa-enable-documentation.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/numa-enable-documentation.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: numa-enable-documentation" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/numa-enable-documentation.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/numa-enable-documentation.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"numa-enable-documentation","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

requirement: '## Context

  Operators enabling NUMA-aware scheduling in YARN need clear guidance about prerequisites, topology sources, and the configuration choices involved before they can turn the feature on safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  The documentation should explain when NUMA awareness is appropriate, what executor prerequisites apply, how to enable it, and how the NodeManager can discover or accept NUMA topology information.


  ## Acceptance signals

  An operator can use the shipped guidance to enable NUMA awareness deliberately, choose the intended topology source, and understand the required configuration points without hunting through implementation details.

# Using GPU On YARN
# Prerequisites

- As of now, only Nvidia GPUs are supported by YARN
- YARN node managers have to be pre-installed with Nvidia drivers.
- When Docker is used as container runtime context, nvidia-docker 1.0 needs to be installed (Current supported version in YARN for nvidia-docker).

# Configs

## GPU scheduling

In `resource-types.xml`

Add following properties

```
<configuration>
  <property>
     <name>yarn.resource-types</name>
     <value>yarn.io/gpu</value>
  </property>
</configuration>
```

In `yarn-site.xml`

`DominantResourceCalculator` MUST be configured to enable GPU scheduling/isolation.

For `Capacity Scheduler`, use following property to configure `DominantResourceCalculator` (In `capacity-scheduler.xml`):

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| 	yarn.scheduler.capacity.resource-calculator | org.apache.hadoop.yarn.util.resource.DominantResourceCalculator |


## GPU Isolation

### In `yarn-site.xml`

```
  <property>
    <name>yarn.nodemanager.resource-plugins</name>
    <value>yarn.io/gpu</value>
  </property>
```

This is to enable GPU isolation module on NodeManager side.

By default, YARN will automatically detect and config GPUs when above config is set. Following configs need to be set in `yarn-site.xml` only if admin has specialized requirements.

**1) Allowed GPU Devices**

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| yarn.nodemanager.resource-plugins.gpu.allowed-gpu-devices | auto |

  Specify GPU devices which can be managed by YARN NodeManager (split by comma).
  Number of GPU devices will be reported to RM to make scheduling decisions.
  Set to auto (default) let YARN automatically discover GPU resource from
  system.

  Manually specify GPU devices if auto detect GPU device failed or admin
  only want subset of GPU devices managed by YARN. GPU device is identified
  by their minor device number and index. A common approach to get minor
  device number of GPUs is using `nvidia-smi -q` and search `Minor Number`

# NUMA Awareness for containers on Node Manager

## Prerequisites

- NUMA awareness is only supported by the `LinuxContainerExecutor`.
- The `numactl` package (which provides the `numactl` binary) needs to be
  installed on every NodeManager host that will run containers with NUMA
  awareness enabled.
- Enabling NUMA awareness makes sense only on hosts that actually have more
  than one NUMA node. On single NUMA node hosts, there is nothing to bind to
  and the feature provides no benefit.

## Enabling NUMA awareness

To enable NUMA awareness for containers on a NodeManager, set the following
property in `yarn-site.xml`:

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.enabled | false |

When enabled, each container launched by the `LinuxContainerExecutor` is
bound, via `numactl`, to one of the NUMA nodes discovered (or configured, see
below) on the NodeManager host. Containers are assigned to NUMA nodes in a
round-robin fashion so that container load is spread evenly across the
available NUMA nodes.

## NUMA topology

The NodeManager needs to know the NUMA topology (the number of NUMA nodes and
the memory/CPUs available on each of them) of the host it is running on. This
topology can either be discovered automatically from the operating system, or
supplied explicitly through configuration.

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.read-topology | false |

If `yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.read-topology` is set to `true`, the
NodeManager reads the NUMA topology from the system by running the command
`numactl --hardware`.

If `yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.read-topology` is set to `false` (the
default), the NodeManager reads the NUMA topology from the following
configuration properties instead:

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.node-ids | (none) |

`yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.node-ids` is a comma separated list of NUMA
node ids present on the host, for example `0,1`. For every id listed, the
memory (in MB) and the number of CPUs of that NUMA node must also be
specified using:

* `yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.<NODE_ID>.memory`
* `yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.<NODE_ID>.cpus`

For example, if `yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.node-ids=0,1`, the following
properties also need to be specified:

```xml
<property>
  <name>yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.node-ids</name>
  <value>0,1</value>
</property>
<property>
  <name>yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.0.memory</name>
  <value>73717</value>
</property>
<property>
  <name>yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.0.cpus</name>
  <value>4</value>
</property>
<property>
  <name>yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.1.memory</name>
  <value>73727</value>
</property>
<property>
  <name>yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.1.cpus</name>
  <value>4</value>
</property>
```

## The `numactl` command

The path to the `numactl` binary that YARN uses to bind containers to a NUMA
node can be configured with:

| Property | Default value |
| --- | --- |
| yarn.nodemanager.numa-awareness.numactl.cmd | /usr/bin/numactl |

Change this property if `numactl` is installed at a non-default location on
the NodeManager hosts.
